correctness.rationale: The four-state labeled de Bruijn Boolean relation R_w has a cycle iff output w repeated bi-infinitely is attainable; R_w^m has a diagonal iff a predecessor of period dividing m|w| exists. A four-vertex directed cycle has a simple cycle of length 1,2,3 or 4, each dividing 12. Rule 90 output 1 forces factor 4; Rule 30 output 1 forces factor 3 and output 011 forces factor 2, making global 12 minimal. Every attainable relation among 256 rules is exhausted by a terminating finite right-multiplication closure of the Boolean 4x4 monoid. Two independent implementations verify exact powers and agree on counts {1:156,2:82,4:6,6:12}, exceptional-rule lists and full table; a separate direct cyclic-input census cross-checks n<=3 for every rule. No inference from finite rings replaces the monoid exhaustion.

value.rationale: The invariant is the least cyclic volume enlargement ensuring that each attainable periodic output has a cyclic predecessor. An all-period exact classification for every elementary rule resolves the natural 256-rule family, distinguishes no-inflation rules from precisely two-, four-, six-fold ones, and gives a sharp universal factor 12. This permits exact finite-volume representation of any full-shift periodic output and is not a one-off finite sample or arbitrary parameter slice.
